stories.headline: Finns Party 'Kiihdytysajot' event: Purra attacks SDP, unveils dandelion logo, hardens immigration line
stories.summary: Finance Minister Riikka Purra held a Finns Party event ('Acceleration Races') in Helsinki, sharply attacking SDP leader Antti Lindtman, unveiling a new dandelion party logo, calling for constitutional changes on immigration, and pledging no further welfare cuts while vowing strict immigration conditions for future coalitions. SDP reacted immediately, accusing Purra of factual distortions.

stories.summary: Kokoomus unveiled a draft 92-page long-term policy programme ('Vapaus onnistua') at its party council meeting on 9 May, proposing to divide municipalities into two tiers, cap family benefits, make some higher-education degrees fee-paying, and expand debt-brake proposals. PM Orpo presented the programme and promised to reveal coalition-level savings plans by autumn 2026.

stories.headline: Government prepares emergency session on hantavirus; Orpo says pandemic risk low but response ready
stories.summary: Prime Minister Orpo announced the government was ready to convene an emergency session from Monday 11 May to classify the Andes-type hantavirus as a dangerous contagious disease, after two Finns were identified as potentially exposed on a cruise ship. THL confirmed two individuals had not yet been tested; Orpo said the pandemic risk was assessed as small.

stories.headline: Orpo's employment statistics claim disputed in parliament; SDP demands correction
stories.summary: PM Orpo claimed in parliament during the public finance framework debate that the number of employed people in Finland was 'almost the same' as when his government took office. Statistics Finland data showed employment was actually 64,000 lower than in June 2023; SDP demanded a correction and Orpo acknowledged his statement was 'perhaps overly open to interpretation.'

stories.headline: Finnish-Ukrainian drone production cooperation accelerates; Ukrainian drones also violated Finnish airspace
stories.summary: Defence Minister Häkkänen met Ukrainian Defence Minister Fedorov and announced acceleration of a joint drone production programme proposed by President Zelensky, while also strongly condemning incidents in which Ukrainian drones strayed into Finnish airspace in recent weeks. The Finnish Border Guard confirmed the drones were likely Ukrainian; the Finnish Defence Forces said they had not shot them down due to proximity to the Russian border.

stories.summary: PM Orpo delivered Finland's EU policy address at Aalto University on 8 May, arguing Europe must develop economic, defence and foreign policy strength, warning that values without power cannot be defended. Orpo referenced Russia's war in Ukraine and shifting US engagement, and announced Finland would host a European Arctic Summit in autumn 2026.

stories.headline: German President Steinmeier makes state visit to Helsinki; Stubb praises Germany's defence build-up
stories.summary: German Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier visited Helsinki on 7 May 2026, meeting President Stubb and PM Orpo. Stubb praised Germany's expanding military as strengthening the whole of Europe, and said the US is not withdrawing from Europe but shifting the burden. The pair also visited a civilian bomb shelter in Helsinki.

Coverage focused heavily on Stubb and Pavel's morning jog with Olympic athlete Kristiina Mäki and footballer Kaan Kairinen, prompting analysis of Stubb's use of sport in diplomacy.

stories.headline: Kokoomus poll ratings slide; Orpo faces internal pressure as SDP widens gap
stories.summary: A new Uutissuomalainen poll showed Kokoomus support continuing to slide, with internal party sources giving candid assessments of Orpo's leadership challenges. A separate USU survey found Left Alliance's Minja Koskela rated the most successful party leader, while Orpo's ratings had declined from October 2025. IS Extra reporting cited anonymous insiders on the root causes.

stories.headline: Orpo condemns May Day protest violence; backs mask ban at demonstrations
stories.summary: PM Orpo condemned a violent assault on a female protester in Tampere on May Day and expressed support for tightening the mask ban at public demonstrations. Interior Minister Rantanen (Finns Party) called for a broader mask ban in all public places; Orpo stopped at banning masks specifically at demonstrations.

stories.summary: Former Labour Minister Arto Satonen published a book detailing his ministerial tenure, disclosing that Orpo called him during his mother's funeral to offer a cabinet post, and that breaking the tripartite labour negotiation model was a Kokoomus objective from the outset of coalition negotiations. Satonen also denied the party acted solely on behalf of the EK employers' federation.

stories.summary: The €55 million, two-year renovation of Mäntyniemi, the official presidential residence, was completed in early May 2026, and President Stubb and Suzanne Innes-Stubb announced they would move in the following week. The renovation incorporated Finnish contemporary art and preserved original interiors.

stories.summary: The Finnish government approved the sale of Fingrid Class B shares worth €62.4 million to OP Pohjola Kantaverkko Holding, as part of a broader restructuring begun in February 2026. Finance Minister Purra stated the deal brings state revenue without weakening state control or ownership position in the electricity grid operator.

stories.headline: Orpo at EPC summit in Yerevan: Finland assesses Ukraine drone cooperation and Ukraine EU membership
stories.summary: PM Orpo represented Finland at the 8th European Political Community summit in Yerevan, Armenia on 4 May, attending a Ukraine support meeting with Zelensky, Starmer, Macron and others. Orpo chaired a connectivity working group, discussed Ukraine sanctions, drone cooperation and potential EU membership, and said there is no reason to delay a possible Finland-Ukraine drone deal.

stories.headline: Bank of Finland publishes China economy forecast; board visits US Federal Reserve
stories.summary: The Bank of Finland's Institute for Emerging Economies (BOFIT) forecast China's real GDP growth at around 4% in 2026, supported by exports while domestic consumption remains weak. The Bank of Finland's supervisory board also made a visit to the US Federal Reserve and IMF in Washington DC and New York on 3-8 May. A separate household savings dashboard was also launched.

stories.summary: A joint survey by Finnish think-tanks Sitra and EVA found that 77% of Finns support the EU reducing economic and technological dependency on the US and China, even if this affects bilateral ties. Researchers noted this reflected strategic concern rather than direct anti-Americanism.

Putin's Victory Day parade on 9 May was notably smaller than previous years, with no missile systems displayed, which Western analysts interpreted as signalling weakness.
